etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Latin refractārius (“obstinate”), from refrāctus, past participle of refringere (“to break up”). Originally refractary, refractarie, but reanalysed after other adjectives in -ory.
senses: Obstinate and unruly; strongly opposed to something.
A material or piece of material, such as a brick, that has a very high melting point.
A plant or factory that produces such material.
